sentences.az: Maşını götürə bilərsən, bir şərtlə ki, bu gün qaytarasan.

sentences.en: Teachers should provide feedback on students' work.
sentences.az: Müəllimlər tələbələrin işləri haqqında rəy bildirməlidirlər.

usage: Two patterns with the same meaning: provide somebody WITH something ("The school provides students with books") and provide something FOR somebody ("The school provides books for students"). Not: "provide students books". PROVIDE is more formal than GIVE and is typical of reports and essays. PROVIDED THAT introduces a condition and is slightly more formal than "if".

expressions.usage: claim = a statement that something is true
moral = giving encouragement rather than practical help
charity = an organisation that helps people in need
Fixed phrase: speak in support of a plan
government = the group of people who rule a country

sentences.en: There is no evidence to support this claim.
sentences.az: Bu iddianı təsdiqləyən heç bir sübut yoxdur.

sentences.en: Which team do you support?

usage: SUPPORT covers several Azerbaijani verbs: dəstəkləmək (support a plan), azarkeşlik etmək (support a team, British English), dolandırmaq (support a family) and əsaslandırmaq (support an argument with facts). The noun is uncountable: "a lot of support", not "a support". In essays, "support your opinion with examples" is a key instruction. SUPPORTIVE describes people who give help and encouragement.

expressions.usage: puzzle = a game or problem that tests your thinking
mystery = something that is difficult to explain
crisis = a time of great difficulty; plural: crises
effective = producing the result that is wanted
conflict = a serious disagreement or fight

sentences.en: There is no obvious solution.
sentences.az: Göz qabağında olan bir həll yolu yoxdur.

usage: You SOLVE a problem, a puzzle, a mystery or a crime, but you ANSWER a question and you RESOLVE a dispute (resolve is more formal). The noun SOLUTION takes TO: "a solution TO the problem" (not "of"). Common verbs with solution: find, offer, propose, come up with. In chemistry, a SOLUTION is a liquid in which something is dissolved.

expressions.usage: accident = a sudden event causing damage or injury

sentences.en: You should avoid eating late at night.

sentences.az: İzdihamdan uzaq olmaq üçün tez çıxdıq.

sentences.en: To avoid confusion, please write clearly.
sentences.az: Anlaşılmazlıq olmasın deyə, zəhmət olmasa, aydın yazın.

usage: AVOID is followed by a noun or by the -ing form: "avoid sugar", "avoid making mistakes". The infinitive is wrong: not "avoid to make". AVOID means to keep away from something; PREVENT means to stop something from happening at all (prevent an accident, prevent somebody from doing something). UNAVOIDABLE describes things that cannot be prevented: an unavoidable delay.

expressions.usage: pain = the feeling when part of your body hurts
effect = a change produced by a cause
root = the origin of a problem
disease = an illness with a specific name
injury = physical harm to the body

sentences.en: The heavy snow caused chaos on the roads.
The news caused great concern among parents.
sentences.az: Bu xəbər valideynlər arasında böyük narahatlıq doğurdu.

sentences.en: Poverty is the root cause of many social problems.
sentences.az: Yoxsulluq bir çox sosial problemin kök səbəbidir.

usage: As a verb, CAUSE usually has a negative object: cause damage, problems, pain, an accident. For good results, use "bring about", "lead to" or "result in". Patterns: cause something; cause somebody something ("cause him pain"); cause somebody TO do something. As a noun, note the prepositions: the cause OF a problem, but a reason FOR something. CAUSE is what makes something happen; REASON is the explanation given.

expressions.usage: worth = having value; be worth + noun / -ing
joint = done by two or more people together
determined = having decided firmly to succeed

desperate = ready to do anything because the situation is so bad
rescue = saving people from danger; plural "efforts" = organised activity

sentences.en: The project was a joint effort between two universities.
sentences.az: Layihə iki universitetin birgə səyi idi.

sentences.en: The company cut prices in an effort to increase sales.
sentences.az: Şirkət satışları artırmaq məqsədi ilə qiymətləri endirdi.

usage: The basic collocation is MAKE an effort (not "do"): "make an effort to arrive on time". EFFORT is uncountable when it means energy in general (It takes effort) and countable for a particular attempt (a determined effort). The plural EFFORTS often means organised work: rescue efforts, peace efforts. "In an effort to" is a useful formal alternative to "in order to try to".

expressions.usage: Without thinking, because you always do it

expressions.az: bir şeyi etməyə vərdiş etmək, adətkar olmaq

regular = happening often or at the same time each day

sentences.en: He has an annoying habit of interrupting people.
sentences.az: Onun insanların sözünü kəsmək kimi əsəbiləşdirən vərdişi var.

sentences.en: She is in the habit of getting up early.
My grandfather is a creature of habit: he has lunch at one o'clock every day.
sentences.az: Babam vərdişlərindən əl çəkməyən adamdır: hər gün saat birdə nahar edir.

usage: A HABIT is something one person does regularly, often without thinking (a bad habit, eating habits). A CUSTOM is a traditional practice of a society (a local custom). Both can be "adət" in Azerbaijani, so choose carefully. Verbs: have a habit, get into / develop a habit, break / kick a habit. The pattern is "a habit OF doing something", not "a habit to do".

expressions.usage: unique = being the only one of its kind

sentences.az: Kurs tələbələrə ingilis dilini məşq etmək imkanı verir.

sentences.en: Don't miss this golden opportunity.
She seized the opportunity to study abroad.
sentences.az: O, xaricdə təhsil almaq fürsətindən istifadə etdi.

sentences.en: I will call you at the first opportunity.

usage: OPPORTUNITY and CHANCE are close, but OPPORTUNITY is more formal and always positive: a situation in which it is possible to do something you want. CHANCE also means possibility or luck ("There is a chance of rain", "by chance"); OPPORTUNITY cannot be used that way. Do not say "a possibility to do": say "an opportunity to do" or "a chance to do". Verbs: have, get, take, seize, miss, give, offer.

exciting = causing great interest and enthusiasm
belief = something you think is true

Climate change poses a major challenge to all countries.

sentences.en: I am sure she will rise to the challenge.
sentences.az: Əminəm ki, o, bu sınaqdan üzüağ çıxacaq.

sentences.en: The new job is difficult, but I find it challenging.
sentences.az: Yeni iş çətindir, amma mənə maraqlıdır.

usage: A CHALLENGE is something difficult that tests your ability, and the word is positive compared with PROBLEM or DIFFICULTY: people "enjoy a challenge". The usual verb is FACE a challenge; also meet, accept, rise to, overcome. As a verb, CHALLENGE means to question whether something is right (challenge a decision) or to invite somebody to compete (challenge him to a game). CHALLENGING is a polite, positive way to say "difficult".

expressions.usage: work under pressure; be under pressure TO do something
peer = a person of the same age or status
blood = the red liquid in your body
air = the mixture of gases around the Earth
resist = refuse to accept or be changed by

sentences.en: I work well under pressure.
Teenagers often start smoking because of peer pressure.
sentences.az: Yeniyetmələr çox vaxt yaşıdlarının təsiri ilə siqaret çəkməyə başlayırlar.

sentences.en: He has high blood pressure.
How do you cope with the pressure of exams?

usage: PRESSURE is uncountable in most uses ("a lot of pressure"), though the plural appears in "the pressures of modern life". Key verbs: PUT pressure ON somebody (to do something), be / come UNDER pressure, cope with / handle pressure, relieve / take the pressure off. PRESSURE comes from outside (a boss, exams, deadlines); STRESS is the feeling inside you that results from it.

expressions.usage: behaviour = the way a person acts
deny = say that something is not true

sentences.en: Who is responsible for this department?
Parents are responsible for their children's safety.
The company denied responsibility for the accident.
sentences.az: Şirkət qəzaya görə məsuliyyəti boynuna almadı.

sentences.en: She has a strong sense of responsibility.

usage: RESPONSIBLE has two uses. Before a noun it means sensible and reliable: "a responsible person". After a verb with FOR it means in charge of, or to blame for: "responsible for sales", "responsible for the damage". The spelling ends in -IBLE, not -able. Noun patterns: TAKE responsibility FOR something; have a responsibility TO somebody. Azerbaijani "cavabdeh" and "məsuliyyətli" are both RESPONSIBLE.

expressions.usage: confident ABOUT the future / the exam

expressions.az: kiməsə və ya nəyəsə inanmaq, etibar etmək

expressions.usage: reasonably = to a fairly high degree
tell somebody something in confidence = as a secret

sentences.en: I feel confident about the exam.
Passing the test really boosted my confidence.
She is not confident enough to speak in public.
sentences.az: O, camaat qarşısında danışacaq qədər özünə inamlı deyil.

sentences.en: I am telling you this in confidence.

usage: CONFIDENT describes a feeling of being sure, either of yourself ("a confident speaker") or of a fact ("I'm confident that we will win"). Prepositions: confident ABOUT / OF something, confidence IN somebody. Do not confuse CONFIDENT with CONFIDENTIAL (secret): "in confidence" belongs to that second meaning. Verbs with CONFIDENCE: gain, build, boost, lose, lack, restore.

expressions.usage: illness = the state of being ill

expressions.az: bir şeyə ciddi yanaşmaq, ciddi fikirli olmaq

expressions.usage: attempt = an act of trying to do something

sentences.en: Her father is in hospital with a serious illness.
Is he serious about leaving his job?
Pollution is a serious threat to our health.
I have serious doubts about this plan.
sentences.az: Bu planla bağlı ciddi şübhələrim var.

usage: SERIOUS means bad or dangerous with problems (a serious illness, a serious mistake), and sincere, not joking, with people ("Are you serious?"). SERIOUSLY is common in three ways: with adjectives for bad states (seriously ill), in "take something seriously" (bir şeyə ciddi yanaşmaq), and at the start of a spoken sentence to show you are not joking. For large amounts, use "considerable" or "significant", not "serious".

expressions.usage: alarm = a clock or signal that wakes or warns you
Phrasal verb: set up a company / a meeting
Phrasal verb; set out to do = start with a clear aim
Phrasal verb: set aside time for study

expressions.az: səhnəni hazırlamaq; ümumi vəziyyəti təsvir etmək
expressions.usage: scene = the place where something happens

We set off early to avoid the traffic.

sentences.az: O, iyirmi beş yaşında öz şirkətini qurdu.

sentences.en: Try to set aside some time for reading every day.
sentences.az: Hər gün mütaliə üçün bir az vaxt ayırmağa çalış.

usage: SET is irregular and never changes: set – set – set. Its core idea is "put something in a fixed position or state": set a date, set a limit, set a record, set an example. With particles it forms very common phrasal verbs: set off (leave), set up (establish), set out (begin with a purpose), set aside (save). As a noun, a SET is a group of things that belong together: a set of keys, a chess set.

expressions.usage: marathon = a race of about 42 kilometres
Phrasal verb: run away from home
Phrasal verb: We have run out of milk
Idiom; long = lasting a great amount of time
errand = a short trip to buy or deliver something
run FOR + position = try to be elected

sentences.en: She runs her own business.
We have run out of petrol.
I ran into an old friend at the airport.
sentences.az: Hava limanında köhnə bir dostuma rast gəldim.

sentences.en: It will save you money in the long run.
sentences.az: Bu, uzun müddətdə sənə pul qənaət etdirəcək.

usage: RUN is irregular: run – ran – run. Beyond the physical meaning, three uses are essential: 1) manage or organise – run a business, run a course; 2) operate – "The engine is running", "run a program"; 3) of transport – "The buses run every ten minutes". Phrasal verbs: run out of (have none left), run into (meet by chance), run away (escape). "In the long run" contrasts with "in the short run".

expressions.az: ağlında bir şey olmaq, nəyisə nəzərdə tutmaq

never = not at any time; fixed spoken phrase
Do you mind if I ...? / Do you mind + -ing?
state = the condition somebody is in
British idiom: be in two minds about something
slip = slide; "It slipped my mind" = I forgot

sentences.en: Do you mind if I open the window?
I'm sorry I'm late. – Never mind.
Tea or coffee? – I don't mind.
sentences.az: Çay, yoxsa qəhvə? – Mənə fərqi yoxdur.

sentences.en: I'm in two minds about accepting the job.
sentences.az: İşi qəbul edib-etməmək barədə tərəddüd edirəm.

usage: As a noun, MIND is the part of you that thinks and remembers; it is close to "ağıl" and "fikir", not to BRAIN (the physical organ). Key idioms: change your mind (fikrini dəyişmək), make up your mind (qərara gəlmək), keep / bear in mind (yadda saxlamaq). As a verb it means to object: "Do you mind + -ing?" is a polite request, and the polite positive answer is "No, not at all". "Mind the gap!" is a warning.

expressions.az: bir işlə məşğul olmaq, həll etmək, öhdəsindən gəlmək
expressions.usage: The key phrasal verb: deal with a problem / a customer
Spoken; said when you accept an offer

sentences.en: How do you deal with difficult customers?
The two companies have struck a deal.
I'll cook if you wash the dishes. – It's a deal!
sentences.az: Sən qabları yusan, mən yemək bişirərəm. – Razılaşdıq!

sentences.en: The staff are trained to deal with emergencies.
sentences.az: Heyət fövqəladə vəziyyətlərin öhdəsindən gəlmək üçün təlim keçib.

usage: DEAL is irregular: deal – dealt – dealt, pronounced /delt/. DEAL WITH has three meanings: take action to solve (deal with a problem), do business with (deal with a supplier) and be about (The book deals with war). The noun DEAL is a business agreement; "a great deal of" means "a lot of" and is used with uncountable nouns in formal English: a great deal of money. "It's no big deal" means it is not important.
